standing: off-board investigation only (owner's ruling docs/b1q_session3_audit_2026_09_07.md); no port opened, no board contact, no re-run, no budget change, no ruling
question: why did B1Q attempt 3 (2026-09-06-03) lose the epoch to PROTOCOL_CRC_BUDGET while attempt 2 passed and the L6 soak survived 2 hours

b1q_2026-09-06-01.end: PROTOCOL (the TERM lost; budget was 2 before v2.4)

loss_shape.evidence: each CRC-failing line, diffed against its intact retransmission, is SHORTER by 1..6 bytes; the payload stays inside the base64url alphabet; no out-of-alphabet byte and no changed-in-place byte appears
loss_shape.per_loss: attempt 1 TERM (not retransmitted), attempt 3: REC seq 3 -1 byte at payload offset 896 (retransmitted intact), HB seq 2 token -6 chars, AUDIT seq 4 -2 chars, plus one SIGNREQ head torn into a MERGED/TORN fragment
loss_shape.reading: small scattered dropped bytes on the receive path, characteristic of a USB-serial RX drop, not electrical line corruption (which flips bytes) and not a large-block buffer overflow

timing_correlation.finding: every real CRC drop lands a fraction of a second AFTER a host->board transmission
timing_correlation.b1q_all_sessions: 5/5 real drops within 0.06-0.25 s of the preceding host TX (IDENTACK/AUDITDONE/SIGNOK/AUDITGET/RECACK)
timing_correlation.l6_soak: 40/40 real drops within 0.5 s of a host TX (100%)
timing_correlation.reading: a full-duplex interaction: the board->host RX bytes are dropped while / just after the host is driving the board<-host TX line, on the CH340 full-speed link through WSL vhci_hcd; not board-side, not random

attribution.ch340_vs_usbip: not yet separable: the CH340 (12M full-speed) and the FTDI JTAG pod (480M high-speed) both traverse vhci_hcd; the FTDI channels are not physically wired to the board UART, so they cannot be A/B'd without rewiring
attribution.prior_evidence: CLAUDE.md records the CH340-over-usbipd path as unstable (brownout drop, ghost-stuck ttyUSB, unstable across detach/reattach)

why_the_soak_survived_and_b1q_did_not: the transport's real byte-loss rate is low on average (~0.017%/frame) but bursty (attempt 3 saw ~1%/frame for 15 s); the 2-hour soak absorbed 40 drops against a budget of 934 over 233k frames, while a 9-probe B1Q session has ~300 frames and a CRC budget of 4 (noise allowance 2 + the two forced seq-1 controls), i.e. a real-noise margin of 2 that a burst exhausts
not_a_fix: raising the B1Q budget (owner's explicit exclusion): it would trade the PROTOCOL-death ceiling for a false PASS on a genuinely noisy link, and does not address the transport

options_for_the_owner.name: budget counts only UNRECOVERED transport failures
options_for_the_owner.where: host: l6_console budget accounting + the plan/prereg semantics
options_for_the_owner.effect: a corrupt frame that the protocol then recovers (a REC retransmitted intact on RECGET, an AUDIT chunk re-pulled intact) no longer counts toward PROTOCOL_CRC; only a loss that is never recovered does
options_for_the_owner.attempt3_would_have: still LOST (3 real drops, of which the HB is fire-and-forget and unrecoverable and the AUDIT pull hit the ceiling); does not save attempt 3 but removes the brittleness for the common single-recovered-drop case
options_for_the_owner.cost: changes the instrument's protocol contract and the frozen plan/prereg; needs its own review, prereg change and manifest
options_for_the_owner.risk: widening what a session tolerates is a measurement-integrity decision, not a bug fix

options_for_the_owner.name: change the physical console transport
options_for_the_owner.effect: move the console off the CH340 (12M full-speed) onto the FTDI pod's spare high-speed UART, or off WSL usbipd onto a native-Linux host, to remove the implicated path
options_for_the_owner.cost: rewiring (the FTDI channels are not wired to the board UART) or an environment move; a new compatibility review of the transport

options_for_the_owner.name: characterise the transport passively before deciding
options_for_the_owner.where: board (needs a ruling: opening the port is board contact)
options_for_the_owner.effect: measure the byte-loss rate and its TX correlation over a longer idle/quiet capture to size any budget or confirm the full-duplex hypothesis
options_for_the_owner.cost: a board session under its own ruling
options_for_the_owner.risk: consumes board time; still on the same transport

recommendation: the finding is a transport fault (option B addresses the cause; option A only softens the symptom and does not save attempt 3); the choice among A/B/C is the owner's. No change is made by this diagnosis.
